text_blocks.snippet: Central Illinois residents face several active and evolving scams reported by local law enforcement, community banks, and state agencies:

list.snippet: U.S. Attorney’s Office & Law Enforcement Scams: Scammers are spoofing official phone numbers belonging to federal and local authorities—including the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of Illinois and the Illinois State Police—claiming victims have missed jury duty, active warrants, or unpaid fines, and demanding immediate payment or personal details.

Bank Impersonation Calls: Community banks across Central Illinois (such as Fisher National Bank and Federated Bank) have issued warnings about callers pretending to be bank security or fraud investigators telling customers their accounts are compromised.

AI-Generated Voices: Fraudsters in counties like Peoria are utilizing artificial intelligence to clone voices, making emergency family-in-distress calls or fraudulent pitches sound shockingly realistic.
Romance Scams: Con artists spend weeks or months building online relationships with local residents before fabricating emergencies that require wiring cash or sending gift cards.

Phishing text messages falsely claim recipients owe unpaid tolls, traffic tickets, or vehicle registration fees, threatening license suspensions or legal action if a payment link isn't clicked immediately.
Note: Official state portals like the Illinois Secretary of State (ILSOS) state they never send text messages demanding money or threatening license revocation (they only send appointment reminders).

Purse & Wallet Thefts: Smash-and-grab or distraction thefts in grocery store parking lots and stores (such as recent incidents reported by Champaign County Crime Stoppers) lead to immediate fraudulent charges at nearby retailers like Target and Best Buy.
Contactless / Tap-to-Pay Fraud: Unofficial solicitors or fake donation drives use rogue tap-to-pay devices to drain thousands of dollars from victim debit and credit cards.

Hang up and call back: Never trust caller ID. If someone claims to be from your bank, law enforcement, or a government agency, hang up and dial the official public number listed on their verified website.
Never pay via gift cards, crypto ATMs, or wire: Government agencies and banks will never ask you to pay fines or secure accounts using unconventional payment methods.

Report suspicious activity: You can track or submit local reports via the Better Business Bureau Central Illinois Scam Tracker or file a federal report with the Federal Trade Commission Fraud Reporting Portal .
